look_here_first: Inspect full MID-STEM leaf shape and its TWO surfaces, then the SIDE of the involucre. C. undulatum tends to have gray-white wool beneath and relatively broader ovate/lanceolate stem leaves that are entire, coarse-toothed or shallowly lobed (not necessarily deeply feather-cut). In larger heads the involucre is often >3 cm; inspect a resinous/glutinous ridge down outer/middle phyllary midveins. For hard undulatum vs ochrocentrum calls, mature cypselae ~6–7 mm with body and rim same color, plus leaf division and wing extent, are useful.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Cauline leaves mainly ovate to lanceolate, often entire or coarsely toothed or shallowly lobed (variable); gray-white wool on lower face. A strongly wavy margin is NOT universal or a single-species proof.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Large purple discoid heads, usually on evident peduncles.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Lanceolate and spine-tipped; larger involucres can exceed 3 cm.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: Broader ovate/lanceolate upper stem leaves: unlobed/coarsely toothed/shallowly lobed in FNA key.; Lower leaf surfaces woolly gray-white; gray color alone shared with ochrocentrum and western Cirsium.; Outer/mid phyllaries may have a longitudinal glutinous resin ridge, seen best by wet/dry macro.; Involucres of larger heads often >30 mm; photograph without corolla with ruler.; Mature cypselae about 6–7 mm long; apical collar roughly same color as fruit body.; Contrast C. ochrocentrum with stronger phyllary spines and decurrent wings in some forms; avoid absolute wing-only key.

lookalikes.differences: Undulatum: broader subentire to shallowly lobed cauline leaves, woolly undersides, often large involucre, mature cypselae ~6–7 mm with concolorous apical rim. Ochrocentrum may have conspicuous decurrent spiny stem wings, longer phyllary spine tips and woolly herbage; forms overlap. Vulgare shows unique short bristle-spines on upper leaf blade. Texanum has considerably smaller involucres.
